solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Female celebrity put up with leers somehow outside government department

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters sit around the department's abbreviation
somehow says these letters get there by some unstated route, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
MOD is the Ministry of Defence, a UK government department

explanation.surface: A famous woman tolerates ogling men while standing outside a Whitehall ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges UP and LEERS into SUPEREL, which goes 'outside' MOD; 'put' and 'with' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: A top fashion model is a famous woman, a celebrity in her own right.

clue.text: Son isn't outlaw — shows such piety

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of isn't
Robin Hood, the legendary English outlaw

explanation.surface: A boy declares he is no criminal, proving his devoutness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' is Robin Hood, the outlaw of English legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being holy or a saint is the extreme of piety; 'such' points back to the saint built by the wordplay.

clue.text: Infant and old man face the camera full of love

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: full of says the pose word holds the zero letter inside it

parts.note: to pose is to sit for a photograph
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A baby and its father smile lovingly for a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American word for a baby, now also the carrier it is strapped in; the clue uses the child sense.

clue.text: Guy has spoken about island on the lord's territory?

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: about says the spoken word wraps round the island's letter

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A man has talked about an island that belongs to a nobleman's estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord's landholding is a manor, so something on it is of the manor; the question mark marks the definition by description.

clue.text: Resident I'd style eccentric, lacking concern

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre, odd, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A local resident calls his own style odd, not caring what others think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges all fifteen letters of RESIDENT I'D STYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without personal interest or involvement; the clue takes the popular sense of not caring, uninterested.

clue.text: Philosopher reading maybe in a secure compartment

parts.note: John Locke, the English philosopher
reading is one of the three Rs, so R is an example of it

explanation.surface: A thinker is perhaps reading in a lockable cubicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so 'reading maybe' gives R; 'in' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lockable cupboard, as in a gym or school, is a secure compartment.

clue.text: Bloke is vulgar, heartless

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the vulgar word is cut out

parts.note: cheap can mean vulgar, tawdry

explanation.surface: A man is described as crude and cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes E, the middle letter of CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British for a man, like bloke.

clue.text: Island capital always given low grades

parts.note: caps are capital letters, so capital gives cap
ever means always
D and E are low exam grades

explanation.surface: A capital city that is forever handed poor ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but gives CAP, as in caps for capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Verde is an Atlantic island nation off West Africa, here standing for one of its islands as a group.

clue.text: A pleasure trip, we hear, comes as an added extra

indicators.note: we hear says the words are to be taken by their sound

parts.note: a cruise is a pleasure trip at sea

explanation.surface: A holiday voyage comes as a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says A CRUISE is spoken, sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When interest or benefits build up and are added on, they are said to accumulate in this way.

clue.text: Legally gets hold of this person's cash

parts.note: this person is, from the setter's view, is I'm
pounds are money, cash

explanation.surface: Someone declares that the law entitles them to seize this money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person's' is the setter speaking: 'this person is' gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorities seize goods or vehicles under legal power, so they take possession lawfully.

clue.text: Slight sign of affection after firm provides a bit of money

indicators.note: after places the kiss behind the company abbreviation

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a peck is a light kiss

explanation.surface: A company follows a small show of fondness with a modest payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian coin worth a hundredth of a rouble, a small piece of money.

clue.text: Member of hobbit family captured

definitions.meaning: a ..., the family of Pippin in Tolkien's Lord of the Rings
past tense of take, as in seized

explanation.surface: A Tolkien character has been seized.
explanation.definitionFit: Pippin is of the Took clan in Tolkien's Shire, and the word is also the past of take, seized.

clue.text: Meeting zone used very regularly when abroad

indicators.note: abroad means far and wide, scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the word very is taken

explanation.surface: A meeting area was frequently used by people overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes VR from VERY, and 'abroad' rearranges ZONE USED plus VR; 'when' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loan word for an arranged meeting or meeting place.

clue.text: Suffering financially? That's obvious, being given the sack

parts.note: overt means open, plain to see
to be axed is to be sacked from a job

explanation.surface: Someone losing their job plainly is in money trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged too much tax, a burden on one's finances; the question mark flags the playful definition.

clue.text: Reclined, maybe, clutching muscle, and given proper treatment

indicators.note: clutching says the rest word grips the muscle inside it

parts.note: lying back is one way to have rested
pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: Someone lying back, holding a sore muscle, was cared for properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated with due regard or honour, as the dead or the rules are.

clue.text: Support hospital organisations? Not the second time

indicators.note: not the second says only the later of the two time letters is dropped

parts.note: hospitals in the UK National Health Service are run by trusts

explanation.surface: Backing for hospital bodies, but not on a repeat occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: NHS trusts run British hospitals; 'Not the second' removes the second T.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a supporting frame for a roof, or a surgical support belt.

clue.text: Port's edge

definitions.meaning: A small port on the Severn in Gloucestershire
the edge of a blade, its keenness

explanation.surface: The rim of a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sharpness is a small port in Gloucestershire, England; the 's of 'Port's' is a joining piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade's edge is its keenness; the Gloucestershire dock town bears the same name.

clue.text: One keen to change, about to confront past

parts.note: re means about, concerning
former means past, earlier

explanation.surface: A campaigner for change sets about facing history.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformer campaigns for change and improvement.

clue.text: Having crossed river, bed down in rubbish

indicators.note: having crossed says the sleeping word spans the river letter

parts.note: to doss is to sleep rough, bed down

explanation.surface: A tramp crosses a river and beds down among the refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is the waste skimmed off molten metal, hence worthless stuff.

clue.text: Little right with priest meeting temptress — take off duty!

parts.note: R is the short form of right
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
Eve tempted Adam with the apple

explanation.surface: A dutiful clergyman meets a seductress and is told to stand down.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a sentry or worker is to replace them so they can stop duty.

clue.text: Brainy bits produced by church dissenter, the Parisian

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rebel dissents from authority
la is French for the, feminine

explanation.surface: Clever ideas come from a churchgoing nonconformist in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of cerebellum, the part of the brain at the back of the skull, so literally bits of brain.

clue.text: Stories about old bishop? They may be articulated

indicators.note: about says the fibs surround the other pieces

parts.note: stories can mean lies, fibs
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Tall tales about an aged bishop that might be well expressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated' suggests speech, but articulated lorries are trucks with a jointed trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Big trucks with a hinged trailer are called articulated, so these vehicles may be.

clue.text: Middle-distance runner beginning to puff, upset? Examination needed

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters bottom to top

parts.note: a miler runs the mile, a middle distance

indicators.note: beginning to says only the opening letter of puff is used

explanation.surface: A runner starts to wheeze and is upset, so needs a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MILER plus P over to read upwards; 'needed' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary examination, short form, as taken before main university exams.

clue.text: Briefly hold mammal spinning round quite briskly

indicators.note: briefly says the last letter is cut short

parts.note: to allege is to hold or maintain

indicators.note: spinning round says the creature's letters are turned backwards

parts.note: an otter is a river mammal

explanation.surface: Quickly grab an animal twirling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' here means maintain or claim, not grasp; 'Briefly' docks its tail and 'spinning round' turns the animal back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning fairly brisk, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Rugby player acceptable without hesitation

indicators.note: without says the hesitation is taken out

parts.note: proper means acceptable, fitting
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A rugby forward who is decent and decisive.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the props are front-row forwards flanking the hooker in the scrum.

clue.text: Chaste woman loves talking, putting lots off

indicators.note: putting lots off says most of the letters of these words are dropped, leaving a run from the middle

explanation.surface: A pure woman adores chatter, which deters many.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vestal virgins were Roman priestesses of Vesta sworn to chastity; the word now means chaste or virginal.

clue.text: Kill rodents — but there's one left inside home

parts.note: to do someone in is to kill; do is slang for kill

indicators.note: inside says the one and left letters go within the rodents

parts.note: mice are rodents
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Exterminate rodents, though one remains indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal or legal word for the place where someone lives.

clue.text: Drink and energy-containing nuts

indicators.note: containing says the crazy word holds the energy letter

parts.note: nuts means mad, crazy
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A beverage and some nuts packed with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink brewed from fermented honey and water.

clue.text: Services, long ago held for local dignitaries

indicators.note: held says the services keep the old-days word inside them

parts.note: masses are church services
yore means time long past

explanation.surface: Church services were long ago put on for civic notables.
explanation.definitionFit: Female mayors, or mayors' wives, are civic dignitaries in local government.
